body:
WHAT
The /session command prints a plain-text report: time spent inside provider calls versus wall-clock time, lines added and removed by Write/Edit, the current context size (measured from the last request, or '~estimated' before any response) with a per-part breakdown (system prompt, tools, addons, messages), free space and percent of the auto-compact limit, and cumulative token usage per model in the four classes. No dollar cost is printed.

WHY
Without it the user cannot see where a session's time and tokens went, how full the window is, or why compaction is about to fire.

WHERE
engine/core/src/runtime/sessionStats.ts — SessionStats.format(settings, now, breakdown), formatBreakdown(), contextNowValue(), recordDiff(), apiMs, linesAdded/linesRemoved, byModel; ContextBreakdown interface. engine/core/src/runtime/engine.ts — Engine slash-command handler case 'session' emits {type:'session_report', text: stats.format(settings, Date.now(), session.contextBreakdown()) + extensionLines()}; the '/session' entry in the slash-command registry. engine/core/src/runtime/session.ts — Session.contextBreakdown(). engine/core/src/config/pricing.ts — formatDuration().

TEST CHECKLIST
1. SessionStats with apiMs 65000 and startedAt now-120000 formats 'Total duration (API): 1m 05s' and 'Total duration (wall): 2m 00s'.
2. recordDiff('--- a\n+++ b\n+x\n+y\n-z\n') then format() reports '2 lines added, 1 lines removed' (header lines not counted).
3. With contextTokens 0 and a breakdown {systemPrompt:1000, tools:500, addons:0, messages:200, limit:0}, the report shows '~1.7k tokens' with 'estimated' and the 'auto-compaction is off' line; with limit 10000 it shows 'Free space' and '17% of the ~10k auto-compact limit used'.
4. After recordResponse('m1', …) and recordResponse('m2', …), the report has a line per model listing input, output, cache read and cache write, and contains no '$'.
5. Engine.send({type:'user_message', text:'/session'}) emits a session_report event whose text starts with 'Session' and includes the 'Context breakdown' lines from session.contextBreakdown().
